questions.question: 141 is divided into two parts in such a way that the one-eighth part of the first and one-ninth part of the second are in the ratio 5 : 6. Find the first part.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **(1/8)th of first part** to **(1/9)th of second part** = 5 : 6

Ratio of **First part (x)** to **Second part (y)** = (5 × 8) : (6 × 9) = 40 : 54 = 20 : 27

Total units = 20 + 27 = 47 units → 141

1 unit = 141 ÷ 47 = 3

**First part** = 20 units = 20 × 3 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total sum = 141

Let the **First part** be x and the **Second part** be y.

Condition 1: x + y = 141

Condition 2: (x/8) : (y/9) = 5 : 6

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0c7ea2939010c108d8d207a67660052890b5aaf99ba020bf472d9508ed5daf8.png] 

From Condition 2:

⇒ (x/8) ÷ (y/9) = 5/6

⇒ (x/8) × (9/y) = 5/6

⇒ 9x / 8y = 5/6

⇒ x/y = (5 × 8) / (6 × 9)

⇒ x/y = 40 / 54 = 20 / 27

Now, divide 141 in the ratio 20 : 27:

⇒ First part (x) = [20 / (20 + 27)] × 141

⇒ x = (20 / 47) × 141

⇒ x = 20 × 3

⇒ x = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Division Rule

To divide a quantity S in the ratio a : b, the first part is [a / (a + b)] × S and the second part is [b / (a + b)] × S.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of (a : b) and (c : d) is (ac : bd). In this problem, we converted the fractions into a simplified integer ratio.

Proportionality

If a/b = c/d, then it is a simple proportion. Here, we used the cross-multiplication method to isolate the ratio of variables x and y.</p

questions.question: The radius of a cylinder is doubled due to which the volume of the new cylinder also gets doubled. The height of the new cylinder is what percentage of the old cylinder?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radius of a cylinder is doubled.

The volume of the new cylinder is doubled.

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cylinder = πr²h

**Calculation:**

Let the original radius be r and the original height be h.

Volume of original cylinder = πr²h

The radius of the new cylinder = 2r

Let the height of the new cylinder be hₙₑw.

Volume of the new cylinder = π(2r)²hₙₑw

Volume of the new cylinder = 4πr²hₙₑw

According to the given condition, the volume of the new cylinder is doubled.

⇒ 4πr²hₙₑw = 2πr²h

⇒ 4hₙₑw = 2h

⇒ hₙₑw = 2h / 4

⇒ hₙₑw = h / 2

The height of the new cylinder is 50% of the old cylinder.

**The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: The average of seven consecutive numbers is 95. Find the middle number in the series of seven consecutive numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any arithmetic progression (like consecutive numbers) with an odd number of terms, the average is exactly equal to the middle term.

Total numbers (n) = 7 (which is odd).

Average of the series = 95.

∴ Middle number = Average = 95.

**∴ The correct answer is 95.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of consecutive terms = 7

Average of terms = 95

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 x−3 x−2 x−1 x x+1 x+2 x+3 
 Middle Term = Average = 95 7 Consecutive Numbers 

Let the seven consecutive numbers be (x − 3), (x − 2), (x − 1), x, (x + 1), (x + 2), and (x + 3).

⇒ Sum of these 7 numbers = (x − 3) + (x − 2) + (x − 1) + x + (x + 1) + (x + 2) + (x + 3)

⇒ Sum = 7x

⇒ Average = Sum ÷ 7

⇒ 95 = 7x ÷ 7

⇒ x = 95

The middle number in the series is x.

⇒ Middle number = 95.

**∴ The correct answer is 95.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression (AP)

For any series in AP, the Average = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2. In this case, (92 + 98) ÷ 2 = 95.

Middle Term for Even Number of Terms

If there are n terms and n is even, the average is the mean of the two middle terms: [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2.

Consecutive Odd or Even Numbers

For consecutive even or odd numbers, the common difference is 2. The property that the average of an odd number of terms equals the middle term still applies.

questions.question: The number of heads on the farm, as determined by the farmer, was 60. When he counted, he discovered there were 150 legs. If all that was present were pigeons or horses, and every horse on the property had four legs while every pigeon had two, how many horses were there on the property?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The number of heads = 60

The number of legs = 150

Each horse has 4 legs.

Each pigeon has 2 legs.

**Formula Used:**

Let the number of horses be H and the number of pigeons be P.

Total heads = H + P

Total legs = 4H + 2P

**Calculation:**

From the given information:

H + P = 60

4H + 2P = 150

To solve these equations, multiply the first equation by 2:

2(H + P) = 2 × 60

2H + 2P = 120

Now subtract this equation from the second equation:

4H + 2P - (2H + 2P) = 150 - 120

⇒ 2H = 30

⇒ H = 15

Using H + P = 60:

15 + P = 60

⇒ P = 45

Therefore, the number of horses on the property is 15.

**The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: Trader A gives a single discount of 45% and Trader B gives two successive discounts of 35% and 10% on an identical item of the same marked price. If the discount given by A is ₹539 more than the discount given by Trader B, then what is the marked price (in ₹) of the item?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Trader A's single discount = 45%

Trader B's successive discounts = 35% and 10%

Difference in discount = ₹539

**Formula Used:**

Discount Amount = Marked Price × Discount Percentage

**Calculation:**

Let the marked price be ₹M.

Discount given by Trader A = 45% of M = 0.45M

Discount given by Trader B:

First discount = 35% of M = 0.35M

Price after first discount = M - 0.35M = 0.65M

Second discount = 10% of 0.65M = 0.065M

Total discount by Trader B = 0.35M + 0.065M = 0.415M

Given difference in discounts:

0.45M - 0.415M = ₹539

0.035M = ₹539

⇒ M = 539 / 0.035

⇒ M = 15400

**The marked price of the item is ₹15400.**

questions.question: Which event brought about a profound change in Ashoka's administrative policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Kalinga War**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kalinga War occurred in 261 BCE and was fought between the Maurya Empire led by Emperor Ashoka and the state of Kalinga (modern-day Odisha).
 
• The war resulted in a massive loss of life and caused significant suffering, deeply affecting Ashoka and leading to his remorse and transformation.
 
• Following the war, Ashoka embraced Buddhism and adopted a policy of non-violence (Ahimsa) and Dharma (moral law) in his administration.
 
• This change is evident in his inscriptions, particularly the Rock Edict XIII, which describes his sorrow over the Kalinga War and his resolve to follow the path of Dharma.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Edicts of Ashoka**

 
 
• Ashoka's edicts are a collection of 33 inscriptions on pillars, boulders, and cave walls, detailing his policies and moral teachings.
 
• They are a crucial source of information on Ashoka's reign and his efforts to spread Buddhism and promote ethical governance.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism and Ashoka**
 
 
• After the Kalinga War, Ashoka became a devout Buddhist and significantly contributed to the spread of Buddhism across Asia.
 
• He sent missionaries to various regions, including Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, and the Hellenistic world.
 
 
 
• **Kalinga**
 
 
• Kalinga was a prosperous and culturally rich region located on the eastern coast of India.
 
• Its strategic location made it a significant target for Ashoka's expansionist policies.
 
 
 
• **Dharma**
 
 
• Dharma in Ashoka's context refers to moral law and ethical principles, which he aimed to incorporate into his administration.
 
• He emphasized principles such as non-violence, compassion, and respect for all life forms.

questions.question: Under which of the following Acts, was Warren Hastings appointed as the Governor-General of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Regulating Act, 1773**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Regulating Act, 1773 was the first act passed by the British Parliament to control the administration of the East India Company in India.
 
• It marked the beginning of parliamentary oversight and introduced significant administrative reforms in the governance of the company.
 
• The Act designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal, with Warren Hastings being the first to hold this position.
 
• The Governor-General was given authority over the presidencies of Madras and Bombay, establishing a centralized administrative structure.
 
• A Supreme Court was also established in Calcutta (now Kolkata) as part of the act to administer justice according to British law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Government of India Act, 1858**

 
 
• This act marked the end of the East India Company's rule and the beginning of direct control by the British Crown.
 
• It transferred the administration of India to the British monarchy, establishing the office of the Secretary of State for India.
 
• The act aimed to improve governance and centralize authority under the British government.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act, 1909**
 
 
• Also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, this act introduced significant changes in the Indian legislative structure.
 
• It expanded the legislative councils at both central and provincial levels and allowed for greater Indian representation.
 
• The act introduced separate electorates for Muslims, a significant development in Indian political history.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act, 1935**
 
 
• This was the longest act passed by the British Parliament concerning the governance of India.
 
• It proposed the establishment of a federal structure in India, including the creation of provinces and princely states.
 
• The act introduced provincial autonomy and expanded the electorate significantly.
 
• It laid the foundation for the eventual independence and partition of India in 1947.

questions.question:
While estimating Gross Domestic Product, the monetary value of only final goods are considered because ________.

a. its immobility, the active economic flow is ended.

b. of the issues of double counting

c. the value added at each stage of the production process is included
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures the economic performance of a country by calculating the total value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given time period.
 
• Only the value of final goods is considered to avoid the issue of double counting, which occurs if intermediate goods are counted multiple times in the production process.
 
• Double counting can lead to an inflated and inaccurate measure of the GDP, as it would count the same value more than once.
 
• Intermediate goods are not included in GDP calculations since their value is already encapsulated in the price of the final goods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**

 
 
• GDP is the total monetary or market value of all the finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.
 
• It serves as a comprehensive scorecard of a country’s economic health.
 
• GDP can be measured using three approaches: production (or output or value added) approach, income approach, and expenditure approach.
 
 
 
• **Final Goods**
 
 
• Final goods are goods that have been completed and are ready for sale to the end consumer.
 
• Examples include cars, household appliances, and groceries.
 
 
 
• **Intermediate Goods**
 
 
• Intermediate goods are products used in the production of final goods or services.
 
• Examples include raw materials like steel, wood, and other components that are used in manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Value Added**
 
 
• Value added refers to the additional value created at each stage of production.
 
• It is the difference between the cost of inputs and the value of outputs.

questions.question: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was built during the reign of the ________ king Narasimhavarman it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pallava**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was constructed during the reign of the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II, also known as Rajasimha.
 
• It is one of the earliest stone-built temples in South India, dating back to the 8th century.
 
• The temple complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its historical and architectural significance.
 
• The Shore Temple is renowned for its Dravidian architectural style and intricate carvings depicting various Hindu deities and mythological scenes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pallava Dynasty**

 
 
• The Pallava dynasty ruled parts of South India from the 3rd century to the 9th century AD.
 
• Their capital was Kanchipuram, a significant cultural and religious center.
 
• The Pallavas were known for their patronage of arts, architecture, and education.
 
• They played a crucial role in the development of Dravidian architecture, as seen in their rock-cut temples and sculptures.
 
 
 
• **Mahabalipuram**
 
 
• Mahabalipuram, also known as Mamallapuram, is a historic town in Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• It is famous for its rock-cut caves, monolithic structures, and temples built during the Pallava period.
 
• The site includes landmarks like the Pancha Rathas, Arjuna's Penance, and the Shore Temple.
 
• Mahabalipuram is a popular tourist destination and a significant archaeological site.
 
 
 
• **Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha)**
 
 
• Narasimhavarman II, also known as Rajasimha, was a prominent Pallava ruler who reigned during the 7th and 8th centuries.
 
• He is credited with the construction of several architectural marvels in Mahabalipuram, including the Shore Temple.
 
• Under his rule, the Pallava kingdom experienced a period of cultural and artistic flourishing.
 
• Rajasimha's contributions to temple architecture have left a lasting legacy in South Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Architecture**
 
 
• Dravidian architecture is a style of temple architecture that emerged in Southern India.
 
• It is characterized by pyramid-shaped towers (vimanas), intricate sculptures, and elaborate carvings.
 
• Prominent examples include the Brihadeeswarar Temple, Meenakshi Temple, and Shore Temple.
 
• This architectural style significantly influenced the construction of Hindu temples across South India and Southeast Asia.

questions.question: Which of the following is a mineral deficiency disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goitre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Goitre** is a condition characterized by the abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland.
 
• It is most commonly caused by an iodine deficiency, which is an essential mineral for thyroid hormone production.
 
• The condition is often seen in areas where the diet is deficient in iodine, such as mountainous regions.
 
• Goitre can lead to symptoms like swelling in the neck, difficulty breathing or swallowing, and hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism.
 
• Prevention includes ensuring adequate iodine intake through iodized salt or iodine supplements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thyroid Gland**

 
 
• The thyroid gland is located in the neck and produces hormones that regulate metabolism, growth, and development.
 
• It uses iodine from the diet to produce thyroid hormones, primarily thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3).
 
• Thyroid hormone levels are crucial for normal brain development, especially during the early stages of life.
 
 
 
• **Iodine Deficiency**
 
 
• Iodine is a trace mineral found in certain foods and is necessary for the production of thyroid hormones.
 
• Deficiency can lead to various health issues, including goitre, hypothyroidism, and developmental abnormalities in children.
 
• Marine foods, dairy products, and iodized salt are good sources of dietary iodine.
 
 
 
• **Hypothyroidism**
 
 
• It is a condition where the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormones.
 
• Symptoms include fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, and depression.
 
• Treatment typically involves hormone replacement therapy with synthetic thyroxine (T4).
 
 
 
• **Hyperthyroidism**
 
 
• It is a condition where the thyroid gland produces excess thyroid hormones.
 
• Symptoms include weight loss, rapid heartbeat, sweating, and irritability.
 
• Treatment may involve antithyroid medications, radioactive iodine therapy, or surgery.

questions.question: Purushottam Dadheech, a renowned Kathak dancer who had been honoured with Padma Shri award for 2020, is associated with which of the following places?

questions.question: With reference to 'slash and burn' agriculture, which of the following names is NOT related to Odisha?

__
 
• **Roca** is not a term associated with slash and burn agriculture in Odisha.
 
• Slash and burn agriculture in Odisha is commonly known by names such as **Bringa, Pama Dabi, and Koman**.
 
• This agricultural practice involves clearing forested land by slashing vegetation and burning it to create fields for cultivation.
 
• The ash from the burned vegetation provides nutrients to the soil, which is used for farming until the fertility decreases.
 
• After the soil's fertility wanes, the land is left fallow, and the cycle is repeated on a new plot of land.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slash and Burn Agriculture**

 
 
• This is a traditional method of agriculture where natural vegetation is cut down and burned as a method of clearing the land for cultivation.
 
• It is also known as **shifting cultivation** due to the shifting nature of crop fields.
 
• Commonly practiced in regions of Latin America, Africa, and Southeast Asia, besides some parts of India.
 
• While it can be sustainable when practiced by small communities with long fallow periods, it can lead to deforestation, soil degradation, and loss of biodiversity when done extensively.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**
 
 
• Slash and burn agriculture can result in the release of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.
 
• It can also contribute to soil erosion and a loss of soil fertility over time.
 
• Increased deforestation due to this practice can lead to habitat loss for many species.
 
• Efforts are being made globally to find more sustainable agricultural practices to replace slash and burn methods.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Alternatives**
 
 
• Agroforestry: Integrating trees and shrubs into crop and livestock farming systems.
 
• Crop Rotation: Alternating crops in a field to maintain soil fertility and reduce pest and disease problems.
 
• Conservation Agriculture: Techniques such as minimal soil disturbance, maintaining soil cover, and crop diversification.
 
• Organic Farming: Using natural processes and materials for farming to maintain soil health and ecological balance.

questions.question: Epilepsy is a disorder that affects which of the following parts of the human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brain cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Epilepsy is a neurological disorder primarily affecting the **brain cells**.
 
• It is characterized by recurrent, unprovoked seizures due to abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
 
• Seizures can vary from brief and nearly undetectable to long periods of vigorous shaking.
 
• Epilepsy can be caused by various factors including genetics, brain injury, or other underlying health conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seizure Types:**

 
 
• Seizures are broadly classified into two categories: focal (partial) seizures and generalized seizures.
 
• Focal seizures originate from one area of the brain, while generalized seizures affect both hemispheres.
 
 
 
• **Diagnosis:**
 
 
• Diagnosis typically involves neurological exams, EEG (electroencephalogram), and imaging tests like MRI or CT scans.
 
• These tests help identify the underlying cause and the type of epilepsy.
 
 
 
• **Treatment:**
 
 
• Treatment options include anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs), lifestyle changes, surgery, or neurostimulation devices.
 
• The choice of treatment depends on the type of seizures, their frequency, and the individual's overall health.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Life:**
 
 
• Epilepsy can significantly impact daily life, affecting education, employment, and social interactions.
 
• Proper management and support can help individuals lead fulfilling lives despite the condition.

questions.question: Which of the following options has all vector quantities?

options.text: Force, Velocity, Momentum, Energy and Power
Force, Velocity, Momentum, Energy and Acceleration
Power, Momentum, Energy, Speed and Work
Force, Velocity, Momentum, Weight and Acceleration

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Force, Velocity, Momentum, Weight and Acceleration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Force** is a vector quantity as it has both magnitude and direction. It is defined as an interaction that, when unopposed, will change the motion of an object.
 
• **Velocity** is a vector quantity that denotes the rate of change of position with respect to time and specifies both magnitude and direction.
 
• **Momentum** is a vector quantity defined as the product of an object's mass and its velocity, indicating the amount of motion an object has.
 
• **Weight** is a vector quantity because it is the force exerted on a body due to gravity, which has both magnitude and direction (towards the center of the Earth).
 
• **Acceleration** is a vector quantity that describes the rate of change of velocity with respect to time, including both magnitude and direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scalars vs Vectors**

 
 
• **Scalars** are quantities that are fully described by a magnitude (or numerical value) alone, such as mass, speed, energy, and work.
 
• **Vectors** are quantities that are described by both a magnitude and a direction, such as force, velocity, acceleration, and momentum.
 
 
 
• **Direction Importance in Vectors**
 
 
• Direction is crucial for vector quantities as it determines the specific way in which the quantity acts, which can impact the resultant effect when combined with other vectors.
 
• Vector quantities can be represented graphically by arrows, where the length of the arrow indicates the magnitude, and the direction of the arrow shows the direction of the vector.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Vectors in Physics**
 
 
• Vectors are essential in physics for describing various phenomena such as force, motion, and fields (gravitational, electric, magnetic).
 
• Understanding vector quantities is fundamental in mechanics, electromagnetism, and fluid dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Vector Addition and Subtraction**
 
 
• Vectors are added or subtracted using graphical methods like the head-to-tail method or by breaking them into components and adding the respective components algebraically.
 
• The resultant vector is obtained by combining these components, which gives a complete picture of the overall effect of the combined vectors.

questions.question: According to Article ______ there shall be equality of opportunities for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 16 of the Indian Constitution ensures **equality of opportunity in matters of public employment**.
 
• This article prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence or any of them in respect of employment or office under the State.
 
• It specifically provides that no citizen shall be ineligible for, or discriminated against in respect of, any employment or office under the State on these grounds.
 
• Article 16 also allows for the provision of reservations for backward classes who are not adequately represented in the services under the State.
 
• It is a crucial part of the **Fundamental Rights** guaranteed by the Constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights**

 
 
• The Fundamental Rights are a set of rights guaranteed to individuals against the State, enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They are considered essential for the development of the individual and the country.
 
• These rights are justiciable, meaning they are enforceable by the courts.
 
• Any law violating these rights can be declared null and void by the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**
 
 
• These principles are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, which means they are not enforceable by the courts.
 
• However, they are fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to create a social framework for the State to follow.
 
• They act as guidelines for the creation of a just society in India.
 
 
 
• **Reservation Policy**
 
 
• India's reservation policy is a form of affirmative action designed to improve the well-being of backward and under-represented communities.
 
• It includes reservations in education, employment, and political representation.
 
• The policy aims to ensure adequate representation and equal opportunities for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and Other Backward Classes (OBCs).
 
• Reservations are provided under various articles of the Constitution, including Articles 15(4), 16(4), and 46.
 
 
 
• **Equality Before Law**
 
 
• Article 14 of the Indian Constitution guarantees that every person shall be equal before the law.
 
• It states that the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• This principle is fundamental to the rule of law and ensures that no individual or group is above the law.
 
• It forms the basis for ensuring justice and fairness in the legal system.

• Mica is a type of mineral that falls under the category of **non-metallic minerals**.

questions.question: The model of 'Quasi Federal' form of government in Indian constitution is borrowed from which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Canada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term "Quasi Federal" refers to a system of governance that incorporates both federal and unitary elements.
 
• India's quasi-federal structure is inspired by the Canadian model of governance.
 
• Canada's constitution provides a federal system with a strong central government while allowing provincial autonomy.
 
• In the Indian context, the central government holds significant power, but states have their own jurisdiction over certain matters.
 
• This blend ensures a balance between the central authority and regional autonomy, similar to the Canadian federal system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Federalism**

 
 
• A system of government where power is divided between a central authority and constituent political units.
 
• Promotes unity while accommodating regional diversity.
 
• Examples include the USA, Canada, Australia, and India.
 
 
 
• **Unitary System**
 
 
• A system of government where a single central authority holds the majority of the power.
 
• Local governments, if they exist, derive their authority from the central government.
 
• Examples include the United Kingdom and France.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List**
 
 
• In India's constitution, it comprises subjects where both the central and state governments can make laws.
 
• In case of conflict, central law prevails over state law.
 
• Examples of concurrent subjects include education, marriage and divorce, and bankruptcy and insolvency.
 
 
 
• **Residual Powers**
 
 
• Powers that are not explicitly listed in the constitution are granted to the central government.
 
• This concept ensures that the central government can legislate on new and unforeseen matters.

questions.question: Which of the following social organisations was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arya Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati on **10 April 1875** in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• The primary aim of Arya Samaj was to reform Hinduism by eliminating orthodox rituals and promoting the teachings of the Vedas.
 
• Swami Dayananda Saraswati's motto for Arya Samaj was "Krinvanto Vishwam Aryam," which means "Make the World Noble."
 
• Arya Samaj was instrumental in promoting social reforms such as women's education, widow remarriage, and the abolition of the caste system.
 
• The organization also played a significant role in the Indian independence movement by fostering a sense of nationalism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Dayananda Saraswati**

 
 
• Born on 12 February 1824 in Tankara, Gujarat.
 
• He was a prominent Hindu religious leader and the founder of the Arya Samaj.
 
• His ideologies were based on the teachings of the Vedas and he advocated for the return to the Vedic way of life.
 
• He wrote the book "Satyarth Prakash," which translates to "The Light of Truth," outlining his religious philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Vedas**
 
 
• The Vedas are a large body of religious texts originating in ancient India.
 
• There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda.
 
• They are composed in Vedic Sanskrit and form the oldest layer of Sanskrit literature.
 
• The Vedas are considered the oldest scriptures of Hinduism and contain hymns, philosophy, and guidance on rituals.
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms by Arya Samaj**
 
 
• Abolition of child marriage and promotion of widow remarriage.
 
• Advocated for women’s education and gender equality.
 
• Emphasized on the removal of untouchability and caste discrimination.
 
• Promoted the use of Hindi and other regional languages in education.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj’s Role in Indian Independence**
 
 
• Arya Samaj members actively participated in the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• Many of its leaders were involved in the Swadeshi movement and the boycott of British goods.
 
• The organization fostered a sense of nationalism and pride in Indian culture and heritage.
 
• It also opposed British colonial policies and worked towards social and educational reforms.
